transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. What brought me in is... well, I keep hearing a man's voice. I work as a mechanic, and I hear him coming from the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes even from right under the hood of the cars. It sounds as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He just keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and... telling me not to touch certain cars.
How long have you been hearing this man's voice? Has this been going on for weeks, months, or longer?

It's been going on for months. I'd say... about ten months now. That's when I first started hearing him. And, well, it's also when I started having these beliefs that I was being tracked. So yeah, both the voice and the tracking stuff have been happening for about ten months.
During these ten months, have there been any periods of time—say, two weeks or longer—when you weren't hearing the voice or experiencing the tracking beliefs at all?

No, they haven't really stopped at all. Even... well, there was a quieter few weeks a little while back where I was just sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't making all those huge plans I sometimes make... but even then, I still heard the voice in the garage. And I still knew my husband and my boss were tracking me. It's just been pretty constant.

You mentioned making huge plans sometimes—can you tell me more about that? During those times when you were making big plans, did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual, and did you have a lot more energy and confidence than your normal self?

Yes, exactly. There was a stretch where I was getting maybe two or three hours of sleep a night, but I felt completely fine. I had all this energy, and I was convinced I could completely reorganize the whole shop, take on double the repairs, just... do everything. I felt really good, really capable. But even during that time, when I was racing around the shop with all those big plans, I was still hearing the man's voice coming from the vents. And I was still absolutely certain that the battery chargers and the security cameras were being used to watch me.

Before you started having those periods with big plans and high energy, had you already been hearing the man's voice and believing you were being tracked for some time? Or did those beliefs and the voice start around the same time as when you first felt that high energy and those big plans?

The voice and the tracking started first. I'd been dealing with all of that for a bit before I ever got that burst of energy and started making those huge plans for the shop. 

And, well, like I mentioned a minute ago, it doesn't really matter what my energy levels are doing. Even during those quieter weeks I had, when I was sleeping a lot more and wasn't making any of those big plans, I still heard the voice in the garage. And I still knew for a fact my husband and my boss were tracking me. The tracking and the voice just... they don't stop, whether I have all that energy or not.
During those quieter weeks when you were sleeping more and didn't have those big plans—did your mood feel low or depressed during that time, or did you feel more like your normal baseline?

Yeah, I guess you could say it felt low. It definitely wasn't my normal self. During those stretches, I just... I don't call anyone back. I even skip the church potlucks that I used to help run. I'll just sit in the house, or out in the bay at work, just staring at my tools like I can't make myself care about any of it. So, yeah, it's a pretty low, empty feeling.
During those quieter weeks when you were feeling low and sleeping more—were you still hearing that man's voice clearly in the garage, or did the voice quiet down or go away during that time?

Yeah, I was still hearing it. Like I was saying before, it doesn't matter if I'm feeling really low and just sleeping all the time, or if I have all that energy. Even during those quiet weeks when I wasn't making any big plans and just felt empty, I still heard the man's voice in the garage just as clear. And I still knew for a fact that my husband and my boss were tracking me. None of that ever stops or goes away, no matter how my mood is.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a 10-month history of persistent auditory hallucinations (hearing a man's voice) and delusions (being tracked by husband and boss) that remain constant regardless of mood state. Critically, these psychotic symptoms predate and persist independently of mood episodes. While the patient experiences distinct periods of elevated mood with decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and grandiose plans (manic features lasting weeks), and separate periods of depressed mood with anhedonia and hypersomnia (depressive features), the psychotic symptoms are not confined to mood episodes—they are present and equally prominent during euthymic periods and across all mood states. This pattern of psychotic symptoms that are independent of mood disturbance is the defining feature of schizoaffective disorder, distinguishing it from bipolar disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia. The presence of both manic and depressive mood episodes with concurrent psychotic symptoms meets criteria for F25.0 (Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type).
